title: Midnight deploy triage journal
content:
Context:
- Late-night canary rollout of v3.14.0 -> 3.14.1 (small perf patch + model-serving kernel change).
- Canary (10% traffic) started at ~23:40 PDT on 2026-03-09. By 00:05 several 503s and backend errors observed.
- This doc is a scratch journal: commands I ran, outputs clipped, hypotheses, and next steps.

Timeline / quick notes:
- 23:40 deploy triggered via circleci pipeline (pipeline-id: 28931). PR merged from github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4132 (commit: 6f2a9ad).
- 23:56 first elevated 5xx alarms: route /v1/generate 5xx increase from 0.2% -> 2.3%.
- 23:59 Canary autoscaler started evicting pods in pool-gpu-1 (OOMKilled on x2).
- 00:03 attempted manual rollback to v3.14.0; rollout stuck in CrashLoopBackoff for the pinned replica set.

Commands tried (copied from terminal):
- kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/inference-service --watch\  (hung at "Waiting for rollout to finish: 1 old replicas remaining")
- kubectl describe rs inference-service-6f2a9ad | sed -n '1,200p'\  -> events: FailedCreate, FailedKillPod, insufficient quota, image-pull backoff on some nodes.
- kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | egrep "CrashLoopBackoff|OOMKilled"\  -> inference-canary-6f2a9ad-abcde  CrashLoopBackOff  1/1  OOMKilled  node-gpu-3
- docker pull eu.gcr.io/redwood-images/inference:6f2a9ad\  -> Digest: sha256:aa11bb22cc...
- gcloud container images describe eu.gcr.io/redwood-images/inference:6f2a9ad --show-package-vulnz  (no vuln relevant)
- kubectl logs inference-canary-6f2a9ad-abcde -n inference --previous\  -> stack snippet: \"RuntimeError: KV cache alloc failed: requested 24GB, available 18GB\"

Observed error snippets (copied/pasted):
- \"RuntimeError: KV cache alloc failed: requested 24GB, available 18GB\"
- \"OOMKilled\" on node-gpu-3, node-gpu-4 shortly after
- kubelet event on node-gpu-3: \"eviction threshold reached for imagefs\"
- \"Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to reserve devices: allocation conflict\"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) New build changed memory usage profile for model-serving process (quantization kernel change). Canary config still has max-seq-length default 2048 -> causes larger KV cache allocation. Result: pods request more GPU host memory and get OOM/OOMKill or eviction.
2) Image digest mismatch / corrupted layer leading to different binary deployed on some nodes (some nodes pulled different cached digest -> some nodes OK, others crash).
3) Node-level pressure: imagefs / ephemeral storage almost full causing kubelet evictions and unstable pulls. This could explain FailedCreate.
4) Scheduling conflicts with device plugin (new plugin version in container changed GPU device requests).

Evidence for/against hypotheses:
- KV cache error strongly points to memory allocation (H1). The error includes exact bytes requested.
- docker pull digest matches registry digest for the tag, but some nodes reported image-pull backoff -> suggests transient registry/network issue (H2/H3).
- imagefs eviction event on node-gpu-3 supports H3.
- Device allocation error line supports H4 but less frequent in logs.

Things I tried and immediate outcome:
- Increase replica resource requests/limits to reserve more host memory (patched deployment to request lower model cache by setting REDWOOD_MAX_SEQ=1024) -> rollout created new pods but still some old rs remained. Observed reduced OOMs but not eliminated.
- Manually forced kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=12 -> attempted rollback but ghost pods referenced missing image on one node (image-pull backoff).
- cordon/drain node-gpu-3, restart kubelet -> node recovered, imagefs freed ~6GB, new pods scheduled. Canary stabilized for ~10 minutes then errors resumed.
- Scaled down canary to 0 replicas to stop traffic and reduce pressure.

Outstanding logs to get (next immediate commands):
- kubectl logs -n inference inference-canary-6f2a9ad-abcde -c runtime --tail=500 (collect full stack)
- kubectl describe node node-gpu-3 | sed -n '1,200p' (check imagefs stats, allocatable)
- sudo du -sh /var/lib/docker/* on node (need SRE help) to confirm image layer retention
- gcloud compute ssh node-gpu-3 --command="nvidia-smi -q | head -n 80" (confirm GPU memory usage outside pods)
- registry: verify if tag 6f2a9ad has multi-arch manifests or was re-tagged within window.

Quick reproduction plan (for staging):
- Build artifact with commit 6f2a9ad and deploy to staging with same k8s node affinity and machine type.
- Run load with small prefix cache warmup to provoke KV cache allocations.
- Monitor node imagefs and kubelet eviction thresholds.

Immediate mitigation (done/recommended):
- Scaled canary to 0 to stop customer impact (done).
- Opened JIRA-REL-921, assigned to Diego and Priya for node imagefs cleanup and registry audit.
- Reverted the PR in registry: retagged 3.14.0 -> stable temporarily while we validate memory profile for 3.14.1.

Notes for longer-term fixes / follow-ups:
- Add a CI artifact smoke test that runs a quick allocation test of model KV cache with representative memory usage before tagging release. Failure should block canary promotion.
- Add a k8s liveness probe that introspects KV cache allocation and returns 429/503 early instead of OOM.
- Improve rolling rollback logic in our pipeline to prefer old RS image digest rather than tag when undoing (pin digest).
- Add image garbage collection runbook for node imagefs and a periodic job to free dangling layers on gpu nodes.

Random commands / notes (for myself):
- git rev-parse --short HEAD -> 6f2a9ad
- circleci artifacts download --pipeline 28931 logs.tar.gz
- kubectl get events -n inference --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 80 > /tmp/inference-events-0310.log

Questions to ask on call with SRE/infra tomorrow:
- Are we running image gc frequency on GPU fleets? default is conservative; can we bump?
- Any known registry flakiness around eu.gcr.io in that window?
- Can device plugin allocation reservation be reported per-pod to detect conflicts?
- Can we add guardrails in rollout step that detect sudden OOM spike and auto-scale down canary?

Next steps (my checklist):
- [ ] Collect full pod logs and node info, attach to JIRA-REL-921 (by 2026-03-12 09:00)
- [ ] Reproduce in staging with 6f2a9ad and kernel build flags (by 2026-03-13)
- [ ] Implement small CI smoke allocation test (RFC to eng-serving-runtime)
- [ ] Draft short postmortem if root cause confirmed (tag: release-ops/postmortems)

Notes to self: keep this doc terse and append command outputs as attachments in JIRA, not in Drive (Drive copy becomes large). Save any long logs to GCS and link in JIRA.

End of scratch journal (Maya)
